planned_outcome: Land HMS Lively: Luikov 1D coupled heat-mass transfer model with 3 dimensionless free parameters (Lu Ko Bi) plus x_core and T_oven_eff. Solve the inverse problem from temperature data alone via Levenberg-Marquardt per published methodology. Test whether explicit moisture-transport physics finally addresses the deep-end information limit M13 surfaced.
actual_outcome: Luikov 1D coupled heat+mass forward solver implemented; uncoupled-limit and steady-state sanity pass. Synthetic recovery with different-class generator: RMSE 0.5 deg C, Lu and Bi recover within 30 percent on 4/5 runs. Real-CSV 5-param inverse: median main-bake RMSE 20 deg C, all fixtures hit param bounds (Lu=0.01, Bi=50). 6/7 converge but parameters non-physical. LOO deep-end T1 RMSE median 26.75 deg C — WORSE than M9 Stefan T1 LOO of 9-21 deg C. Adding moisture transport made the inverse harder, not easier. Verdict CONFIRM-information-limit: full physics-class hierarchy (heat eq + Stefan + Zurcher 2-state + Luikov coupled) exhausted; in-dough thermometry alone fundamentally cannot constrain x_core deep-region behaviour. Method 4 is the final path.
success_metric_result: Luikov 5-param real-CSV main-bake RMSE 20 deg C (worse than M9 Stefan 5-11 deg C); LOO deep-end RMSE 26 deg C (worse than M9 Stefan 9-21 deg C); 0/7 fixtures with params in literature ranges; 4 model classes now exhausted.

adopt: Test forward-solver sanity in TWO regimes — both an uncoupled limit and a long-time steady-state — to catch implementation bugs in coupled-PDE solvers
avoid: Adding more model complexity (more parameters, coupled state vars) when the previous LOO test already showed information-limit; complexity makes the inverse harder when data is information-limited
